name: Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary Art
funding: State: Ural branch of the National Centre for Contemporary Arts, part of the Pushkin Museum since 2020; 6th edition (2021) budget c. 100m RUB; residencies sought Presidential Fund for Cultural Initiatives grants.
watch: 7th edition cancelled in Apr 2023 (announced by the city administration without explanation); team shifted to a research platform and art-industrial routes (2025 routes to Nov 2025). Founder-commissioner Alisa Prudnikova left to run GES-2 (V-A-C).
records_note: No records of its own were reachable, so this is its parent, the Pushkin Museum: yearly reports and accounts, logo-only sponsors, named trustees.

name: Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Municipal autonomous institution; founder Department of Culture of the Yekaterinburg city administration; Hermitage-Ural centre opened 2021.
watch: No partners page on the site (404); no controversy found.
records_note: It posts yearly reports 2014 to 2023, financial results 2014 to 2024 and the supervisory board's composition orders, but no sponsor list.

name: NTU Centre for Contemporary Art Singapore
funding: Nanyang Technological University research centre; EU-funded SEA AiR residency; public research grants. Budget not found.
watch: Exhibition space reduced in 2021; roster not checked. No donor list published, only research grants with funders unnamed. Exhibitions and residencies halted Mar 2021 after Economic Development Board funding ended.
records_note: No records of its own; parent NTU posts annual reports 2016 to 2026 with audited accounts; the centre lists its Governing Council.

name: National Gallery Singapore
funding: State funding plus corporate donors; DBS and UOB name galleries.
watch: Current patrons include casino operator Marina Bay Sands plus Bloomberg and Citadel, both on the campaign list.
why_flagged: Current patrons include casino operator Marina Bay Sands plus Bloomberg and Citadel, both on the campaign list.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports for 2009 to 2025 with a financial report, names its patrons including Marina Bay Sands, and lists its board.

name: MGLC International Centre of Graphic Arts
funding: Funded by the City of Ljubljana; organises the Ljubljana Biennale of Graphic Arts.
records_note: It lists its Board of Trustees and a founding-supporters roll from its creation, posts no annual reports, and its AJPES filings were not opened.

name: Origins Centre
funding: Wits campus museum, opened 2006; its Rock Art Research Institute is funded by the National Research Foundation, Wits' research fund and Anglo American's Chairman's Fund. No centre funder list.
watch: The draft's Arcadia and arts-department funding has no source.
records_note: The centre has no records of its own; parent Wits University posts annual reports 2006 to 2025 with audited accounts and lists its Council.

name: Busan Biennale
funding: 2026 edition run by the Busan Biennale Organizing Committee for Busan Metropolitan City, with BNK Busan Bank, Shinsegae, Naver and Danish, Dutch and UK cultural funds.
records_note: It posts yearly public-interest settlement filings for 2023 to 2025 and names its officers and auditors, but no annual reports or sponsor list.

name: Changwon Sculpture Biennale
funding: 2024: 107,710 visitors; run by Changwon City and Changwon Culture Foundation; backed by Culture Ministry, Gyeongnam, KICOX and BNK Kyongnam Bank.
watch: Roster not checked. 2026 edition (30 Sep-15 Nov) is open; its supporter list was not found. The 2024 roster stands. Names include BNK Kyongnam Bank and Gyeongnam Mecenat Association.
records_note: Parent Changwon Culture Foundation posts accounts 2016 to 2025 and officer rosters, but no annual reports or funder list.

name: National Asian Culture Center (ACC)
funding: Government agency of Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism that plans and spends its own budget; operations are shared with the ACC Foundation.
watch: State-funded; roster not checked. The only criticism found is governance (the two-part set-up), not sponsors.
records_note: Its site posts yearly introduction brochures and programme guides but no financial reports, funder list or board.

name: Alternative Space LOOP
funding: Non-profit association (2019); 2026 shows supported by Arts Council Korea, supervised by Seoul Metropolitan Government, plus individual LOOP's Friends donors.
watch: Roster not checked. Dec 2025 Euljiro move drew a public gentrification inquiry from Cheonggyecheon-Euljiro Preservation Alliance and others.
records_note: Its Support page names its chairs, directors, auditor and 44 individual donors, undated, but it posts no reports or accounts.

name: Arko Art Center
funding: State-run: operated by Arts Council Korea (national arts body, est.
watch: State-funded; roster not checked. Parent Arts Council Korea gave grant juries a political blacklist of artists in 2015; exposed in a National Assembly inspection.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Arts Council Korea posts reports 2019 to 2025, lists its council and files accounts on ALIO.

name: Fundació Antoni Tàpies
funding: Private foundation with Catalan public support.
records_note: It posts annual reports of activities for 2025 and 2026, audit reports 2015 to 2024, a grants table to 2025 and names its trustees.
